neet_che_u06_t12_1.working: CH3COONa is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base. CH3COO- hydrolyses to give OH-, so the solution is basic. NH4Cl and CuSO4 give acidic solutions; NaCl gives a neutral one.

neet_che_u06_t12_2.working: For a salt of a weak acid and strong base, pH = 7 + 1/2(pKa + log C) = 7 + 1/2(5 - 2) = 8.5.

neet_che_u06_t12_3.working: Kh = Kw/Kb = 1e-14/1e-5 = 1e-9. h = sqrt(Kh/C) = sqrt(1e-9/0.1) = sqrt(1e-8) = 1e-4.

neet_che_u06_t12_4.working: For a weak acid–weak base salt, pH = 7 + 1/2(pKa - pKb). This has no concentration term, so dilution barely changes the pH. A is false and R is true.

neet_che_u06_t12_5.working: Statement I: for CH3COONa, h = sqrt(Kh/C), so dilution increases the degree of hydrolysis; I is incorrect. Statement II: for CH3COONH4, h is independent of concentration, but Kh = Kw/(KaKb) depends on temperature; II is incorrect.
